module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1043

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1043](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1043)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., Metric properties of polynomials. J.
  Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Po59] Pommerenke, Ch., On some problems by Erdős, Herzog and Piranian. Michigan Math. J.
  (1959), 221-225.
- [Po61] Pommerenke, Ch., On metric properties of complex polynomials. Michigan Math. J. (1961),
  97-115.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1043

open MeasureTheory Polynomial

/-- The set $\{ z \in \mathbb{C} : \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ -/
def levelSet (f : Polynomial ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  {z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1}

/--
**Erdős Problem 1043**:
Let $f\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ be a monic polynomial.
Must there exist a straight line $\ell$ such that the projection of
$$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$$
onto $\ell$ has measure at most $2$?

Pommerenke [Po61] proved that the answer is no.

The projection onto the line $\ell = \mathbb{R} u$ is measured with the Lebesgue measure of that
line, so `volume` of the projected set is its length.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 28 30,
formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos1043.lean",
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/XC0R/formal-conjectures/blob/7db17471701f15b125d1c36bc1fa5bb9b702d6be/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1043.lean#L214"]
theorem erdos_1043 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.degree ≥ 1 →
      ∃ (u : ℂ), ‖u‖ = 1 ∧
      volume ((ℝ ∙ u).orthogonalProjectionOnto '' levelSet f) ≤ 2 := by
  sorry

/--
On the other hand, Pommerenke also proved there always exists a line such that the projection has
measure at most 3.3.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 28 30]
theorem erdos_1043.variants.weak :
    ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.degree ≥ 1 →
      ∃ (u : ℂ), ‖u‖ = 1 ∧
      volume ((ℝ ∙ u).orthogonalProjectionOnto '' levelSet f) ≤ 3.3 := by
  sorry

end Erdos1043

reformulations.difference: The source permits any straight line; Lean parametrizes lines through the origin as ℝ ∙ u with ‖u‖ = 1 and measures the projection within that subspace.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every affine line has the form a + ℝu with ‖u‖ = 1. Its orthogonal projection has arc-length coordinate ⟪u,z−a⟫, which differs from ⟪u,z⟫ by a constant. Translation preserves Lebesgue measure. Moreover, t ↦ t • u is a volume-preserving linear isometry from ℝ onto the line subtype, so the inferred volume is genuinely length. The scratch file proves the projection-volume identity and the universal-bound ↔ allowing arbitrary affine offsets, for any bound c; this applies to c = 2 and hence also under the False ↔ answer wrapper.

reformulations.difference: The bound 3.3 is stated using unit directions and linear subspaces rather than arbitrary affine straight lines.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same translation-invariance and volume-preserving-coordinate argument applies. The generic universal-bound equivalence proved in /workspace/review/validation.lean specializes to c = 3.3, showing that permitting arbitrary affine offsets does not change this claim.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The current source explicitly states the nonconstant-monic hypothesis, the negative answer for bound 2, and the universal bound 3.3; its DISPROVED (LEAN) status agrees with the file. Independent Lean proofs in /workspace/review/validation.lean verify the measure interpretation, affine-line equivalence, projection length exactly 2 for f = X in every unit direction, exclusion of constant polynomials, and the exact identity (3.3 : ENNReal) = 33/10. These proofs use no sorry axioms. EHP58 uses the open sublevel set; its projected lengths agree with those of the closed sublevel set used by the current website and Lean, since only finitely many interval endpoints are added. Full-text access to Po59 and Po61 was blocked; their stated results were checked against the explicit current Erdős page, not independently against their proofs.
